channel.title: EngineerzCorneR — Posts
channel.description: Deep-dive technical write-ups across Electrical, Mechanical, HVAC, Automation, Civil and Solar.

item.title: Resource Loading and Utilization
item.description: How to read resource loading and utilization, why a healthy team average hides overloaded people, and when to use resource leveling or smoothing.

item.title: Change Order Cost and Schedule Impact
item.description: How to price a change order, why only approved changes move the baseline, and when extra work earns time: critical path and float, with worked examples.

item.title: Cable Derating Factors Worked Through
item.description: How ambient and grouping factors multiply into one derating factor, the square-root rule for temperature, and a worked cable selection with the In and Iz check.

item.title: Vessel Purging and Inerting Explained
item.description: Dilution purge turnovers, pressure-swing cycles and NFPA 69 oxygen targets, with worked examples for taking a vessel from air to a safe oxygen level.

item.title: Fractions to Decimals Explained
item.description: Convert tape-measure fractions to decimal inches and millimetres, round decimals to the nearest 1/16, 1/32 or 1/64, and know which results repeat.

item.title: Tank Volume vs Level Explained
item.description: Why horizontal tank level and volume are not proportional, the circular segment formula, and how 2:1, hemispherical and torispherical heads change the answer.

item.title: Contingency vs Management Reserve
item.description: Contingency, management reserve and the project budget stack, AACE estimate classes, and a worked example that turns a risk register into a contingency figure.

item.title: RTD vs Thermocouple Explained
item.description: How Pt100 RTDs and thermocouples measure temperature, IEC 60751 and 60584 tolerance classes, lead and cold-junction errors, with worked examples.

item.title: Pipe Wall Thickness (ASME B31.3)
item.description: ASME B31.3 pressure design thickness, corrosion allowance and the 12.5% mill tolerance, with a worked NPS 6 example and schedule selection.

item.title: Genset Ratings: ESP, PRP, COP, LTP
item.description: ISO 8528-1 ratings ESP, PRP, COP and LTP, average load factor, derating and fuel autonomy, with a worked comparison for the same 320 kW load.

item.title: Insulation Resistance Testing Explained
item.description: IEC 60364-6 / BS 7671 test voltages and minimums, motor spot IR and polarization index per IEEE 43, temperature correction and worked examples.

item.title: Lighting Design Beyond Lux
item.description: EN 12464-1 lux, uniformity and glare targets, room index, layout spacing and EN 1838 emergency lighting, with a worked 6 x 5 m office example.

item.title: SPD & Lightning Protection Explained
item.description: Lightning protection levels, SPD Types 1/2/3, Uc, Up and lead length (IEC 62305, IEC 61643-11), with a worked check against impulse withstand.

item.title: The PPP Project Lifecycle: From Identification to Handback
item.description: The eight stages a Public-Private Partnership moves through, from project identification to handback, and the enablers that hold the whole lifecycle together.

item.title: Pre-Commissioning vs Commissioning: What's the Difference
item.description: Pre-commissioning happens before a system is energized; commissioning happens after. The checks each phase covers, why order matters, and where FAT/SAT fit in.

item.title: Conventional vs. Balanced Bellows vs. Pilot-Operated PSV: Choosing a Relief Valve Type
item.description: Three ways a relief valve holds its disc shut until set pressure — how back pressure and dirty service decide between conventional, bellows, or pilot-operated.

item.title: Reading a Psychrometric Chart: The Five Lines That Matter
item.description: How a psychrometric chart is built from dry-bulb temperature, humidity ratio, relative humidity, wet-bulb temperature, and enthalpy.

item.title: Cavitation in Pumps: Causes, Warning Signs, and Prevention
item.description: What pump cavitation actually is, why NPSH available has to beat NPSH required, the field symptoms that give it away, and a practical prevention checklist.

item.title: Pump & Fan Affinity Laws: Why Speed Changes Cube the Power
item.description: Flow scales linearly with speed, head scales with the square, and power scales with the cube.

item.title: Pump Types Explained: Centrifugal to PD
item.description: What a pump actually does, eight common pump types, key parts, a centrifugal-vs-PD comparison, a selection checklist, and common failure points.

item.title: PV String Sizing: Why Voltage, Not Wattage, Decides Panels Per String
item.description: Why a cold morning can push string voltage past an inverter's limit, how the temperature coefficient drives that swing.

item.title: RACI Matrix Explained: Who's Responsible vs. Who's Accountable
item.description: Why projects stall when nobody owns a decision, what Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed actually mean.

item.title: Rational Method: How Peak Stormwater Runoff Is Estimated
item.description: Q = C × i × A looks simple, but the runoff coefficient, the time of concentration and the design storm behind the intensity decide whether the peak flow you size a pipe for is realistic.

item.title: Rebar Development Length: Why Bar Diameter Decides the Embedment, Not Rules of Thumb
item.description: Why development length is a function of bar diameter and concrete/steel strength, not a flat number, how lap splices scale off it, and what hooks buy you.

item.title: Refrigerant Types: R-410A to A2L
item.description: Why HVAC is transitioning away from R-410A, the ASHRAE 34 safety classification (A1/A2L/B2L), R-32 vs R-454B vs R-1234yf vs natural refrigerants compared by GWP and flammability, what changes for A2L handling, and a selection reference.

item.title: Relay Basics: Construction, Working Principle & Contact Types
item.description: What a relay is, how the coil and armature switch a separate power circuit, NO/NC/CO contact types, common applications, and trade-offs vs solid-state relays.

item.title: Relief Valve Orifice Sizing
item.description: Set pressure, allowable overpressure, back pressure, and required relieving rate — the inputs that decide a relief valve's required orifice area under API 520, and why the scenario matters more than the formula.

item.title: Retaining Wall Components Explained
item.description: What every part of a cantilever retaining wall actually does — stem, footing, toe, heel, shear key, drainage, and reinforcement — component by component.

item.title: Retaining Wall Design Basics: Why Overturning, Sliding & Bearing All Have to Pass
item.description: The three independent stability checks behind every gravity or cantilever retaining wall — overturning, sliding, and bearing pressure.

item.title: Risk Register Basics: Turning Probability × Impact Into Priority
item.description: Why a risk list without scoring is just a list, how Probability × Impact turns gut feeling into a comparable number.
